overall_summary: Space anomalies and cosmic physics paradoxes are the dominant drivers of performance on FACTVERSE. Extreme planetary conditions (such as burning ice, coal-dark atmospheres, and molten iron rain) consistently outperform standard biological trivia and over-saturated psychology topics. Relatable but mind-bending physical paradoxes (like gravitational time dilation affecting head vs. feet aging) also show strong potential when framed around personal relevance.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice Will Break Your Brain!' (1,055 views), 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (963 views), and 'The Planet Where It Rains Molten Iron!' (353 views) represent the channel's highest-performing tier.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on bizarre cosmic phenomena and exoplanets with extreme, highly visual weather or physical properties.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Why Your Head Is Older Than Your Feet' achieved 262 views by framing gravitational time dilation as a personal, mind-bending biological fact.
winning_patterns.action: Produce content that explains complex physics or cosmic laws using the human body or daily life as a reference point.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5 views / 53 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views / 71 views) consistently fail to capture audience interest.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid generic self-help or basic cognitive psychology facts unless they can be tied to a shocking historical mystery or a high-stakes survival scenario.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (118 views / 183 views) and 'The Only Animal That Can Live Forever' (69 views) underperform compared to cosmic topics.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot animal content away from simple textbook facts and toward cinematic survival narratives or bizarre evolutionary anomalies.
